findings.title: [Security Advisory] September 2026 CVE Advisory Notification (KB3159623)
findings.summary_md: ServiceNow's own advisory page carries a published date of 2026-09-23 in its page metadata (modified 2026-09-24) and states that on September 24, 2026 the vendor issued CVE-2026-86857, CVE-2026-86858, CVE-2026-13016, CVE-2026-86859 and CVE-2026-86860. The issues were identified through internal security testing, customer security assessments, or reports submitted through responsible disclosure and bug bounty programs, and each was remediated independently. The advisory notes that researchers who reported issues through responsible disclosure may choose to publish their findings, and that ServiceNow did not identify evidence of malicious exploitation.

findings.title: CVE-2026-13016: ServiceNow AI Platform SQL Injection (NVD record)
findings.summary_md: NVD published the ServiceNow PSIRT record for CVE-2026-13016 on September 24, 2026, describing a SQL injection that could let an unauthenticated user execute arbitrary SQL statements against an instance's underlying database and access or modify data beyond what was intended. Versions before Yokohama Patch 13 Hot Fix 5a, Zurich Patch 10 Hot Fix 3b, Zurich Patch 10 Hot Fix 4a W32, Zurich Patch 11 Hot Fix 3, Australia Patch 2 Hot Fix 4b W32, Australia Patch 4 Hot Fix 3 and Australia Patch 5 are listed as affected, with a vendor CVSS v4.0 score of 9.3 critical. The vendor statement records that the update was deployed automatically to hosted instances while partners and self-hosted customers must apply it themselves, and that ServiceNow is not currently aware of malicious exploitation.
